_about: Coldwater Bench Orchard's answers to every Organic System Plan module, loaded by seed_coldwater_bench and checked against the live questionnaire on every run. A fabricated Washington apple and pear orchard (the rehearsal kit's farm, documentation/gtm-v3/rehearsal/). No real certifier, packer, nursery, supplier, irrigation district or public body is credited with any act: the packer is 'Sample Bench Packing Co.' and the ditch belongs to the fictional 'Sample Bench Irrigation District'. The answers agree with the seeded records, including the ones a reviewer will question: the purchased compost has no paperwork yet, the district's canal treatment is not known, and the calcium chloride is a foliar spray for bitter pit. A module marked not_applicable describes work this orchard does not do (the packer stores and packs the fruit). common_osp_records lists the Common OSP section 11 record types the operator states it keeps.

answers.contract_notes: Coldwater Bench Orchard LLC farms as Coldwater Bench Orchard, above Manson, Chelan County: Block 1 Gala, Block 2 Gala, Block 3 Honeycrisp and Block 4 d'Anjou are bearing; Block 5 Honeycrisp (transition) is a young block bought in November 2024 and not yet bearing. Dan Tollefsen manages the orchard and signs for it; Karen Tollefsen keeps the records and is the contact for the certifier. Records were kept on paper until the 2026 season.
answers.history_prior_agents: Only the agent this plan is filed with. No other agent has certified any part of the orchard.
answers.regulatory_agencies: Dan Tollefsen holds a Washington private applicator license for the orchard's own blocks. No other permit or registration covers organic production here.

answers.fraud_review_process: Karen checks every input invoice against the materials list before the product is used, and checks the packer's organic certificate each January before the renewal goes in. Inputs bought from a hardware store or a county yard (the calcium chloride, the compost) are the weak point: nothing is applied until the bag label or the supplier's sheet is in the binder. The 2026 compost went on before its sheet arrived, and that is listed as an open item for the certifier.
answers.osp_accuracy_process: Karen reads this plan against the spray sheet and the binder each winter, before the March renewal, and updates it when a block, a product or the packer changes.
answers.ofpp_team: Karen Tollefsen, owner and office manager, (509) 555-0147, karen@coldwaterbench.example. Dan Tollefsen, orchard manager and licensed applicator, (509) 555-0147.
answers.record_review_frequency: Weekly in season: Karen reads the spray sheet every Friday. The whole binder each winter, before the March renewal.
answers.supply_chain_description: Inputs come from the farm co-op, a hardware store and a county compost yard. Fruit leaves the farm in our own bins, tagged at the block, on the packer's truck to Sample Bench Packing Co., a certified organic packer that packs, stores and sells it. A small share of Gala is sold loose from bins at the farm stand.
answers.ccp_inputs_strategy: Nothing goes on a block unless it is on the materials list. Karen checks each invoice and label against the list before the product goes in the shed.
answers.ccp_inputs_monitoring: Every invoice when it arrives, and the whole input list against the spray sheet each winter. The 2026 compost came without its feedstock and process sheet; it is on the plan and the paperwork has been asked for.
answers.ccp_transport_strategy: Fruit moves only in our own bins, tagged with the lot code at the block, on the packer's truck. The driver signs the receiving ticket.
answers.ccp_transport_monitoring: Bin counts on our harvest sheet are checked against the packer's receiving ticket for every load.
answers.ccp_sales_strategy: Organic fruit is sold only through the certified packer, which issues the invoices. The packer's organic certificate is checked each January.
answers.ccp_sales_monitoring: Each season the settlement statement is checked against our bin counts by lot; the packer's certificate each January.

answers.seeds_additional_notes: No seed is planted: the orchard floor is resident grass. The trees in all five blocks were in the ground before 2026; no tree was planted or replaced this season.

answers.calcium_chloride_disorder: Bitter pit on Honeycrisp (Block 3): foliar sprays at 4 lb per 100 gal in June and July.
answers.tillage_practices: No tillage in the tree rows or the alleys. The alleys are resident grass, mowed four or five times a season; prunings are flailed in the alleys and left. Compost is spread on the surface along the tree rows and not worked in.
answers.in_lieu_description: Perennial apple and pear blocks with no tillage. Resident grass in every alley, mowed four or five times a season, with prunings flailed in place. Compost spread on the surface along the tree rows of Blocks 1, 2 and 3 on July 15, 2026; Block 4 was not done after the spreader broke, and Block 5 gets none.

answers.soil_fertility_additional_notes: 240 tons of compost from a county yard, spread on Blocks 1, 2 and 3 on July 15, 2026 (Block 4 was not done after the spreader broke). The yard has not yet sent its feedstock and process sheet; it was asked for in writing and is outstanding.

answers.natural_resources_description: A bench above the lake: shallow sandy loam over gravel. Permanent grass covers every alley and the headlands. A poplar row and a 25 ft grass strip run along the north fence, between Block 1 and a neighbor's conventional cherries.
answers.irrigation_water_sources: Blocks 1, 2, 3 and 5: drip from the farm well. Block 4: from the irrigation district's ditch, not the well.
answers.shared_irrigation_mitigation: The ditch also serves conventional orchards downstream; Block 4 takes its water at our own turnout and nothing is injected at the turnout. Whether the district treats the canal is being asked of the district.
answers.irrigation_source_names: Block 4: the Sample Bench Irrigation District ditch. Blocks 1, 2, 3 and 5: the farm's own well.

answers.input_use_conditions: Codling moth: mating disruption dispensers in every block before first flight, then granulovirus covers timed from trap catches. Mites and scale: oil at delayed dormant and again only if mites build in summer. Dormant lime sulfur and copper before bud break. Thrips and other insects only when found on the scouting walk, and only with a material on the materials list.
answers.monitoring_records: Codling moth trap catches and what was seen on the walk are written on the spray sheet beside the spray they led to. In 2026 the trap counts themselves were not kept in the binder; from 2027 they are logged in Trazo against the block.
answers.pests_diseases_of_concern: Codling moth, leafrollers, pear psylla and mites; fire blight and powdery mildew. Bitter pit on Honeycrisp is a calcium disorder, not a disease, and is handled under soil fertility.
answers.pest_prevention_records: The spray sheet notes when the mating disruption dispensers went up in each block, and the trap checks that timed each granulovirus cover. In 2026 the trap counts themselves were not written down.
answers.disease_prevention_records: Disease sprays are on the spray sheet with their dates and blocks. Pruning and the dormant cleanup are done every winter but are not written down.
answers.weed_prevention_records: None written. The alleys are mowed four or five times a season and the tree rows are kept clear without herbicide; neither is recorded by date.

answers.drift_response_procedure: Note the date, what was sprayed and the wind, look for damage on our side of the buffer, keep fruit from the affected rows out of organic bins, and call the certifier before any of it is picked. The June 15, 2026 spraying along the north fence is recorded as a possible incident on Block 1.
answers.dedicated_equipment_contamination_preven: Every block on the orchard is organic or in transition and managed the same way, so the sprayer, tractor and bin trailer only ever work this orchard.

answers.empty_bin_storage: Empty organic bins from the packer are stacked on the gravel pad by the shop until picking starts, away from the north fence.
answers.non_own_transport_records: The packer's truck collects full bins from the orchard. The packer's receiving ticket names the block, the lot code on the bin tag and the bin count; Karen files a copy with the harvest record.

answers.sales_soe_channels: Almost all fruit goes in bins to one certified organic packer, which packs, stores and sells it. A small share of Gala is sold loose from bins at the farm stand for cash.
answers.sales_soe_lot_linkage: Each pick gets a lot code (CB-26-B1-GALA for Block 1 Gala in 2026) written on the bin tags. The packer's receiving ticket and settlement carry it. Stand sales are written in the receipt book by date, without a lot code.
answers.other_venues_detail: Farm stand at the farm, 100 Sample Bench Rd, Manson: organic Gala sold loose from bins. No non-organic products are sold there.

answers.container_lot_linkage_description: The bin tag carries the lot code, which is the block and the variety; the packer's receiving ticket repeats it.
answers.label_claim_review_process: We print no consumer labels; the packer labels the packed fruit under its own certificate. At the stand a hand-written sign says 'Organic Gala' with the farm's name; Dan checks it before the stand opens.

answers.lot_numbering_description: CB-YY-B#-VARIETY: CB for Coldwater Bench, the two-digit crop year, the block number and the variety. Written on every bin tag and carried on the packer's receiving ticket.
answers.lot_code_key: CB = Coldwater Bench. 26 = crop year 2026. B1 to B5 = block number. GALA, HC (Honeycrisp), ANJOU = variety. Example: CB-26-B4-ANJOU is the 2026 d'Anjou pick from Block 4.
answers.records_organic_status_explanation: The Gala sold loose from bins at the farm stand is not written down, so no sales record exists for it. Everything sold through the packer carries its lot code from the bin tag to the settlement statement, which identifies it as organic.
